exposure: Source: whole file read into memory once and hashed; line boundaries found by find(LF). Header: bytes up to and including the 98th LF sliced and split into lines 1-98; every header line blank-stripped and matched as bytes against the dash-separator pattern (header only, K5); lines 10-17 and 30-38 ASCII-decoded and regex-checked. Data lines 99 onward: only bytes 1-41 sliced, before any interpretation; the LF position bounds the slice and decides the boolean "line has at least 41 bytes"; bytes >= 42 touched only by the hash and the LF search, never sliced, decoded, stripped, compared, measured or emitted. Bytes 1-11 of every data line blank-stripped and compared with the two target names; only the two target prefixes tokenized; tokens decoded only after their shape regex matched or, for emission, after every condition passed. CDS ReadMe read, hashed, decoded, tag-stripped; lines 144-216 checked. Manifest read, hashed, JSON-parsed in full; only crosscheck_massmodels.reference_distance_texts accessed; its single string compared by float equality with tokens 2-7 of NGC3198, never emitted or printed. Emitted on success only: five literal tokens per target with byte spans, source line, documented units/semantics, check booleans, assumption states. Never emitted: T, the anchor text, any other row, any byte >= 42. On failure: codes and booleans only.
exposure_correction: Corrects earlier wording. V002 split the whole file into lines (materialising every byte of every data line), searched lines 1-200 for the separator by stripping and matching whole data lines 99-200, and only afterwards kept bytes 1-41 of the target lines; its statement that bytes beyond 41 were never decoded, compared or measured was inaccurate for that separator search. The 0349 census and checker had the same separator search (K5). V003 never materialises a data-line slice longer than 41 bytes and searches for the separator in header lines 1-98 only.
